e: 5 + 7 = 12, write 2 carry 1; then 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. So 42.
7 × 8 = 56 — one of those multiplication facts worth memorising.

q: Half of 90 is?
How many minutes are in 2 hours?
e: 1 hour = 60 minutes, so 2 × 60 = 120 minutes.

q: If x + 3 = 10, then x = ?
e: Subtract 3 from both sides: 10 − 3 = 7.

q: Perimeter of a square with side 5 cm?
e: A square has 4 equal sides: 4 × 5 = 20 cm.

q: Choose the plural of ‘child’.
e: ‘Child’ is irregular: one child, many children.

q: Choose the word nearest in meaning to ‘happy’.
e: Glad and happy both describe feeling pleased.

q: What is the opposite of ‘early’?
e: Early and late are opposites of timing.

q: Which of these letters is a vowel?
e: The vowels are a, e, i, o, u.

q: ‘She ___ to school every day.’
e: With he/she/it the verb takes -es: she goes.

q: Pick the correctly written sentence.
e: ‘I’ is always capital and a sentence ends with a full stop.

q: ‘Book’ becomes ‘books’. This is called the…
e: Adding -s makes most nouns plural (more than one).

q: What is the SI unit of force?
e: Force is measured in newtons (N), named after Isaac Newton.

q: Water boils at what temperature at sea level?
e: At sea level pure water boils at 100°C.

q: Which instrument measures temperature?
e: Thermo = heat, meter = measure: thermometer.

q: The Earth revolves around the…
e: The Earth orbits the Sun once every year.

q: Speed = distance ÷ …
e: Speed is how much distance you cover per unit of time.

q: Which surface absorbs heat best?
e: Dark, dull surfaces absorb (and radiate) heat best.

q: Gravity pulls objects…
e: Gravity pulls everything towards the centre of the Earth — down.

q: What is the chemical formula for water?
e: Two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen: H2O.

q: Which gas do plants take in to make food?
e: Plants absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen.

q: NaCl is the formula for common…
e: Sodium chloride — ordinary table salt.

q: The chemical symbol for oxygen is?
e: Oxygen is simply O; O2 is the gas molecule.

q: The most abundant gas in air is…
e: Air is about 78% nitrogen and only 21% oxygen.

q: The pH of pure water is?
e: 7 is neutral — neither acid nor base.

q: A substance that dissolves in water is called the…
e: The solute dissolves; the water doing the dissolving is the solvent.

q: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
e: The heart is a muscular pump that never rests.

q: Green plants make their food by…
e: Photo = light: plants use sunlight to make food.

q: How many legs does an insect have?
e: Every insect has 6 legs — it is part of the definition.

q: Which organs do we breathe with?
e: The lungs take in oxygen and give out carbon dioxide.

q: The basic unit of life is the…
e: All living things are built from cells.

q: Which blood cells fight infection?
e: White blood cells are the body's soldiers.

q: Which organ digests food?
e: The stomach churns and breaks down what you eat.

q: We live on planet…
e: Earth — the only known planet with life.

q: The main source of energy for the Earth is the…
e: Nearly all Earth's energy starts at the Sun.

q: The three common states of matter are solid, liquid and…
e: Solid, liquid and gas — water shows all three.

q: Which of these conducts electricity?
e: Metals like copper conduct; rubber and plastic insulate.

q: The force that pulls objects towards the Earth is…
e: Gravity is why things fall down, not up.

q: Which tool is used to measure length?
e: A ruler (or tape) measures length in cm and m.

q: The change from liquid to gas is called…
e: Evaporation: liquid water becoming vapour.
